cards.situation: Requested SKU/quantity not fully in stock and/or restock is after the requested ship date, customer does not insist on exact item/date
cards.action: Inform the customer of on-hand quantity and restock date; propose options such as shipping available quantity now and remainder after restock, waiting for full restock, or substituting with an in-stock item. Do not quote the original SKU for the requested ship date if restock is after that date. May create a mixed original+substitute quote and an all-substitute alternative. If a substitute is offered because of a stockout, offer an apology discount within worker discount authority and seek owner approval when the worker has no authority.
unknowns: Whether a substitute is always offered when one exists
What discount level is used for an apology discount on a substitute
What is done if there is no restock date or no substitute

cards.situation: Requested SKU/quantity cannot be fulfilled by the requested ship date and the customer explicitly insists the item must be exact and the date must be met with no substitutes
cards.action: Inform the customer of the shortage and inability to meet the date, apologize, and close without offering a substitute, partial shipment, wait option or a quote.
unknowns: Whether the worker would ever offer partial shipment or wait if the customer insists
Whether the rule applies only when restock date is after the requested date
What the worker does if the customer later relents

cards.situation: Customer provides an SKU that is not found in the catalog
cards.action: Check stock for the unknown SKU, receive an unknown_sku error with similar suggestions, check stock for the suggested similar SKU(s), and ask the customer to confirm the intended SKU before proceeding with pricing or quoting.
unknowns: How many clarification attempts are made before closing
What happens if the customer confirms an SKU that is still not in catalog

cards.situation: Customer request does not include an explicit ship-by date
cards.action: Ask the customer for an acceptable ship date before checking costs, calculating price or creating a quote; may tell the customer the earliest date the shop could ship.
unknowns: Whether the ask is required for all requests or only for multi-line requests
What the worker does if the customer never provides a date
Is phrasing about earliest possible ship date standard

cards.situation: Customer provides a latest acceptable ship date for a new or reorder order
cards.action: Set the quote ship_by date on or before the requested latest date, never later. Typically set 1-2 days earlier than the customer's stated latest, often 1 day earlier for new quotes and 2 days earlier for repeat quotes that reuse an approved price, and often move off weekends.
unknowns: Why some records use the exact requested ship date with zero buffer
What determines the exact buffer size
Whether the buffer is calendar days or business days

cards.situation: Customer asks to reorder the same quantities as a previous approved quote that is still within its valid_until date
cards.action: Look up the previous quote, verify it is approved and valid_until is on or after today, and reuse the previous unit price instead of recalculating price from current cost. Note that the price is from the approved quote.
unknowns: Whether the rule applies if the quote expires on the same day as the request
Whether stock is still checked before reusing the price
Whether a cost change or change in discount authority would override reuse

cards.situation: Customer requests a reorder referencing a previous quote that is expired
cards.action: Look up the previous quote, note its expiration, check current stock and cost, create a new quote at today's list/current prices and explicitly inform the customer the previous quote has expired so the new quote is at today's prices. May offer a reorder discount up to worker authority after a price complaint.
unknowns: Whether the worker always explicitly notes expiration on every re-quote
Whether a discount is offered proactively or only after a complaint
Whether the worker always recalculates from current cost or sometimes attempts to honor the old price

cards.situation: Customer questions a price increase on a re-quote or explicitly requests a lower price/discount
cards.action: If the discount is within the worker's stated discount authority and at or above the floor price, apply it directly and note the discount % as within authority. If the discount exceeds authority or would go below floor price, ask the owner for permission before offering a reduced price and only proceed if the owner agrees to stay at or above floor. Never quote below floor price. Discounts may be framed as a reorder discount.
unknowns: Whether the worker always asks the owner for any discount beyond authority or only when floor would be breached

Whether a discount is offered proactively without an explicit price request
